questions.prompt: Why can a triage that only reads ImagePath miss a malicious svchost-hosted service?
options: ImagePath is encrypted for svchost services
For svchost-hosted services ImagePath is legitimately 'svchost.exe -k <group>' -- the malicious code is in the ServiceDll value one level down under Parameters
ImagePath is not recorded for services
svchost services have no ImagePath at all
questions.explanation: The process genuinely is svchost.exe with a genuine -k argument and a genuine services.exe parent. Only the ServiceDll value under the Parameters subkey reveals what is actually being loaded.

questions.prompt: Why is Event ID 7045 particularly valuable for service-based persistence detection?
options: It requires no audit policy configuration and records service name, image path, and start type at installation
It is only generated on domain controllers
It captures the full binary content of the service
It is written to the Security log with tamper protection
questions.explanation: 7045 is logged by default in the System log by the Service Control Manager, unlike Security event 4697 which depends on audit policy being enabled.

questions.prompt: Why is a 7045 event a useful lateral-movement detection?
options: It only fires during lateral movement
PsExec and similar tools work by installing a service on the target, so a service installation on a machine nobody administers is worth investigating
7045 records the source IP address of the attacker
questions.explanation: Service installation is how PsExec-style remote execution works. The service name is trivially changed, but the installation event itself still fires.

questions.prompt: What does a service Type value of 1 indicate, and why does it matter?
options: An automatic-start service, meaning it runs at boot
A kernel driver, which raises a different set of concerns covered in the BYOVD lesson
A disabled service that can be safely ignored
A service owned by a standard user
questions.explanation: Type 1 means the entry is a kernel driver rather than an application service, which puts it in the vulnerable-driver threat model rather than ordinary service persistence.
